system_description.narrative_title: Middle East conflict triggers global oil & shipping crisis
system_description.narrative_summary: An intensifying Iran-linked conflict—Houthi strikes, tanker attacks and assaults on airports—plus U.S. political restraint ahead of midterm elections and coincident hurricane disruptions are constraining maritime oil and gas flows through the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. Markets, carriers and energy firms are responding with route changes, flight suspensions, production shut-ins and sanctions, producing reinforcing feedbacks that lift prices, strain logistics and reshape short-term energy security decisions.
system_description.scope: Maritime and pipeline flows of crude, refined fuels and LNG through the Gulf/Strait of Hormuz; proxy and state-backed attacks on ships, airports and energy infrastructure; policy and military decision-making by regional and external states; market price formation and corporate operational responses (oil majors, shippers, airlines); short-term weather shocks affecting production and transport.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic energy system (interactions among international security, energy markets and global trade)
adjacent_subsystems: U.S. domestic politics and election timing
Climate and extreme-weather impacts on energy supply
evidence_headlines: Oil gains as Middle East hostilities stoke supply worries
Plane billows smoke at Riyadh airport
Attack risks rise for tankers as Iran vows to block more Hormuz routes
Trump says US will not attack Iran before midterm elections in November
Lufthansa, Indian airlines suspend flights to Riyadh after Houthi attacks
Oil Climbs on Intensifying Shipping Attacks, U.S. Storm Fears

variables.name: Maritime energy flow rate
variables.description: The aggregate rate at which crude oil, refined fuels and LNG are transported through maritime chokepoints and adjacent sea lanes.

variables.name: Refinery operational utilization
variables.description: The average proportion of refining capacity that is operational and processing feedstocks at a given time.

variables.name: Crude oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price level for benchmark crude oil, reflecting supply-demand balance and risk premia.

variables.name: Perceived shipping risk
variables.description: The market and operator assessment of the probability and expected severity of attacks, seizures or other hazards affecting commercial shipping.

variables.name: Tanker capacity available
variables.description: The volume of ocean tanker tonnage that is available and deployable for crude and product transport in global trade lanes.

variables.name: Freight rate level
variables.description: The prevailing freight and charter rate level for transporting oil, gas and refined products by sea.

variables.name: Maritime route closure extent
variables.description: The proportion of key sea lanes and chokepoints that are effectively closed, restricted or avoided for commercial transit.

variables.name: Production shut-in rate
variables.description: The rate at which upstream oil and gas production is taken offline due to security, weather or operational constraints.

variables.name: Insurance premium level
variables.description: The average level of insurance and war-risk premia charged for maritime and aviation operations in affected regions.

variables.name: Strategic stockpile level
variables.description: The aggregated volume of publicly and privately held strategic crude and product inventories available to buffer supply shocks.

variables.name: Corporate operational response intensity
variables.description: The aggregate pace and scale of operational actions by energy and transport firms, including route changes, suspensions and capacity reallocations.

variables.name: Military intervention likelihood
variables.description: The assessed likelihood and expected intensity of external or regional military actions that could alter security conditions for energy flows.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure level
variables.description: The overall intensity and economic reach of trade, financial and shipping-related restrictions applied to actors or routes.

variables.name: Alternative route share
variables.description: The share of transported energy volumes rerouted onto longer or non-standard maritime and pipeline pathways.

variables.name: Weather disruption severity
variables.description: The current severity of weather events (storms, hurricanes, extreme conditions) that disrupt production, shipping and port operations.

variables.name: Market expectation volatility
variables.description: The short-term volatility in market expectations about future supply, demand and policy developments affecting energy and transport markets.

catalysts.title: Hurricane Isaias prompts Gulf shut‑ins
catalysts.description: Landfall and associated storm impacts force U.S. Gulf producers to shut in output and disrupt refinery and port operations in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Hurricane Isaias ... threatens US Gulf production'; 'US Gulf producers shut in more oil and gas as Isaias nears landfall.'

catalysts.title: Escalation of tanker attacks and Hormuz blocking
catalysts.description: Iran-backed attacks and threats to block 'illegal routes' in the Strait of Hormuz drive repeated tanker strikes and expanded route disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Attack risks rise for tankers'; 'Iran attacks tankers beyond Strait of Hormuz'; 'Attacks on tankers ... highest of any week.'

catalysts.title: Post‑midterms U.S. military action window
catalysts.description: Political constraint before U.S. midterms eases afterward, raising the chance of renewed strikes or altered military posture that could affect energy flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump says US will not attack Iran before midterm elections' — implying elevated post‑midterms action risk.

catalysts.title: Accelerated Asian oil stockpiling
catalysts.description: Asian buyers accelerate purchases and strategic builds in response to the Iran war and shipping risks, tightening available market supply.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Asia races to stockpile oil, speed up renewables in response to Iran war.'

catalysts.title: Further sanctions on shadow fleet tankers
catalysts.description: Continued Treasury and allied actions target tankers linked to Iran's shadow fleet, reducing usable tonnage and escalating compliance risk for operators.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Treasury sanctions 17 tankers linked to Iran's "shadow fleet"' — signals further targeting of tankers.

catalysts.title: Tanker scarcity and charter‑rate surge
catalysts.description: Carriers avoid high‑risk Gulf transits, traders and owners scramble for tonnage and charters spike as storage and rerouting demand rises.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Vitol chief warns of tanker shortage'; 'US oil trader takes $2bn gamble on tankers'; 'Ships’ captains paid $100,000 a month.'

catalysts.title: El Niño intensifies — winter weather risks
catalysts.description: UN warning of El Niño through Feb 2027 raises likelihood of extreme weather that will disrupt shipping, ports and production seasonally.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'UN weather body says El Niño set to intensify and last until February 2027.'

catalysts.title: Saudi‑Pakistan‑Turkey mutual defence pact
catalysts.description: New trilateral defence understanding may change regional military dynamics, altering both the likelihood of intervention and operational responses protecting supply lines.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey trigger mutual defence pact' — shifts regional military posture and responses.
